comparison_structure: California mainland + Santa Catalina + Santa Cruz; recent colonization ages known
reason: Higher selfing capacity on islands but no poorer or more variable current hummingbird visitation and no detected current selection for selfing; separates colonization filtering from current reproductive-assurance selection

comparison_structure: northwest Chiloe coastal island population vs Puerto Blest Andean mainland population
reason: Self-incompatible at both sites; visitor assemblages differ strongly and natural-pollination efficiency differs, giving a direct community-context-to-reproductive-output contrast without a historical turnover chain

comparison_structure: nine Newfoundland populations testing predicted island breakdown of heterostyly
reason: Explicit island prediction is retained as falsification: homostyly did not gain the predicted selfing advantage and tested populations remained highly self-incompatible

comparison_structure: 43 Svalbard populations of nine Saxifraga species cultivated in phytotron
reason: Direct Arctic breeding and spontaneous-selfing evidence broadens assurance states, but lacks island-mainland transition and realized community shift

comparison_structure: three Hainan altitude populations with visitor observations and pollination treatments
reason: Pollinator identity changes across altitude; no automatic selfing or apomixis; hand pollination raises fruit set over natural pollination, especially at high altitude

comparison_structure: two sympatric native Goniothalamus species in Borneo
reason: Direct floral biology, pollinator trapping and breeding-system evidence supplies local mechanism depth but not an island-mainland transition

comparison_structure: 15 Central Sulawesi agroforestry systems across forest-distance and local-management gradients
reason: Bee abundance/composition and local-regional filtering predict open-pollinated fruit set; mechanistically strong but crop/agroforestry context is not promoted as natural-island response evidence

comparison_structure: six sympatric dioecious Ficus species and obligate fig-wasp mutualists in New Guinea
reason: Experimental heterospecific pollinator transfers identify contemporary reproductive-isolation mechanism, but provide no island-mainland transition or assurance axis
